(A) AI Module.name: (A) AI Module
(A) AI Module.description: Software connected to an Ur AI core running throughout the ship. Can automate tasks or run the ship on behalf of the crew. Snarky personality module available for free.

(U) Land Rover.name: (U) Land Rover
(U) Land Rover.description: Armored all-terrain vehicle for carrying heavy cargo or folks over land. High-powered winch and decorative stickers come standard.

(Ce) Stun Weapons.name: (Ce) Stun Weapons
(Ce) Stun Weapons.description:
A wide variety of weapons for capturing and securing prisoners without (serious) harm. Includes, but is not limited to:
Restraints. [0 load]
Stun batons. [1 load]
Stun settings on blasters. Not the heavy kind. [1 load]
Stun grenades. Replaces detonator on the sheet. [1 load]
Knockout drugs. May not work on some xenos. [0 load]
Not required to bring on jobs, but useful if you want to claim bounties. Generally legal.

(Fi) Black Market Contacts.name: (Fi) Black Market Contacts
(Fi) Black Market Contacts.description: Able to get you all the modules (even illegal ones) your ship needs, even when you're wanted. Resourceful. Mobile. Illegal modules (as usual) may require you to run a job to acquire them. Your contact may know where to find them, and give you a leg up, but it's up to you to get things that just aren't available at any price (prototypes, rare devices, and incredibly illegal things like coherence cannons).

(C) Nexus Link.name: (C) Nexus Link
(C) Nexus Link.description: A link to the Hegemonic System Network. Allows for news updates, realtime messages, and tapping into system-wide sensor grids. Others may be able to hack into your ship remotely via the same channel.

(A) Shields.name: (A) Shields
(A) Shields.description: Particle sinks and EM deflectors. Overwhelmed by focused fire. Counts as armor against ship weapons and energy attacks. Largely absorbs blaster fire.

(Ce) Hard Knocks.name: (Ce) Hard Knocks
(Ce) Hard Knocks.description: Sometimes luck is just hard-earned experience. Your crew starts each job with +1 gambit.

(Fi) Driven.name: (Fi) Driven
(Fi) Driven.description: Each PC gets +1 trauma box. This can bring a PC with 4 trauma back into play if you wish.

(G) Survival Gear.name: (G) Survival Gear
(G) Survival Gear.description: Camping gear, rebreathers, climbing equipment, scuba gear. Everything an enterprising crew needs to survive on an inhospitable, but not uninhabitable, rock. Stillsuits included.

(H) Cargo Hold.name: (H) Cargo Hold
(H) Cargo Hold.description: Enough space on a ship to make a moderate (cred-earning) shipment. A cargo hold is evident when the ship is boarded, and no special precautions are taken to hide its contents.

(T) Prowess.name: (T) Prowess
(T) Prowess.description: May represent an appropriate place on your ship, relevant manuals, or expert mentors. Mark 2 xp in the appropriate category instead of 1 when taking the downtime train action.

(T) Insight.name: (T) Insight
(T) Insight.description: May represent an appropriate place on your ship, relevant manuals, or expert mentors. Mark 2 xp in the appropriate category instead of 1 when taking the downtime train action.

(G) Alien Pet.name: (G) Alien Pet
(G) Alien Pet.description: Lovable rapscallion or loyal guardian, these critters are more trouble than they're worth.

(C) Targeting Computer.name: (C) Targeting Computer
(C) Targeting Computer.description: Handles calculations and targeting for weapon systems without the crew. Roll comms rating when firing.

(A) Armory.name: (A) Armory
(A) Armory.description: A secure room holding the crew weapons and armor, which are considered fine.

(Ce) Smooth Criminals.name: (Ce) Smooth Criminals
(Ce) Smooth Criminals.description: Sometimes legality is only a question of who has the gun. Each crew member gains +1 stress box (total 10).

(U) Intruder Alarm.name: (U) Intruder Alarm
(U) Intruder Alarm.description: A full suite of sensors about the ship, including motion sensors, door codes, and panic buttons that can all trigger a klaxon and red security lights.

(St) Dark Hyperspace Lane Maps.name: (St) Dark Hyperspace Lane Maps
(St) Dark Hyperspace Lane Maps.description: These are routes through systems that aren't officially maintained. Sometimes they are faster. They are always less patrolled. Often they are full of Way creatures, pirates, and other scoundrels. The ride is never as smooth as it is along the Starsmith-maintained routes. You don't want to think too hard about the poor fools that died or got lost forever mapping these routes.

(Ce) Tracers.name: (Ce) Tracers
(Ce) Tracers.description: A wide array of ways to track your targets. Includes tiny bugs that can be hidden on clothes with a suave pat on the back, beacons that can attach to hulls, and even transmission cloners for comms. Legality varies (often by the importance of the target), but a license makes it all legal.

(W) Mining Drill.name: (W) Mining Drill
(W) Mining Drill.description: Vicious, close-range, high-power energy drill. Vaporizes rock. Easily modified to bore through hulls. Legal.

(W) Missiles.name: (W) Missiles
(W) Missiles.description: Projectile with mounted drive. Not legal.

(A) Brig.name: (A) Brig
(A) Brig.description: Space jail. Not meant for long-term incarceration.

(U) Holo-Emitters.name: (U) Holo-Emitters
(U) Holo-Emitters.description: For holo-conferences and maps. Images won't hold up to close scrutiny but can be convincing for a short while. Includes sweet games and holo-vids.

(St) False Ship Papers.name: (St) False Ship Papers
(St) False Ship Papers.description: Every smuggler needs a few wellforged documents, giving the crew and ship identities that are less wanted in any given system. These papers often simplify gate travel if the transponder and ship match. You have a couple different sets you can swap between, even if you do have to practice responding to a new name at every checkpoint. May make following and tracking you more difficult by enemy factions.

(E) Afterburners.name: (E) Afterburners
(E) Afterburners.description: Dumps raw fuel into the engines for a short burst of speed. May treat engines as one higher rating for a roll, but it may damage them.

(E) Jump Drive.name: (E) Jump Drive
(E) Jump Drive.description: A special engine that can activate the Ur gates that connect systems and translate the ship into hyperspace lanes.

(W) Particle Cannons.name: (W) Particle Cannons
(W) Particle Cannons.description: Pew! Pew! Usually fixed in one direction on personal vessels. Often cross linked. Not legal without license.

(E) Cloaking Device.name: (E) Cloaking Device
(E) Cloaking Device.description: Doesn't necessarily render the ship invisible to the eye, but masks the heat and electrical signature of the ship, making it very hard to detect or identify. Super illegal.

(G) Recon Drone.name: (G) Recon Drone
(G) Recon Drone.description: A small drone for surveillance, mapping, and intelligence gathering. Can be given simple instructions. Uses comms quality when contested.

(T) Resolve.name: (T) Resolve
(T) Resolve.description: May represent an appropriate place on your ship, relevant manuals, or expert mentors. Mark 2 xp in the appropriate category instead of 1 when taking the downtime train action.

(C) Long-Range Scanner.name: (C) Long-Range Scanner
(C) Long-Range Scanner.description: Provides broad EM spectrum and gravimetric readings, giving the crew advance warning up to a dozen light-minutes away.

(Fi) Secret Base.name: (Fi) Secret Base
(Fi) Secret Base.description: Could be inside ancient Ur ruins on a planet. Maybe buildings inside a massive asteroid. Possibly an old and forgotten station, long abandoned but now repurposed. You have found and commissioned a hiding spot away from the baleful gaze of the Hegemony where you and your allies can meet, hide, lick your wounds, and plan your jobs, all without the Hegemony finding out. It's secret...for now.

(U) Vault.name: (U) Vault
(U) Vault.description: Useful for securing valuables during space travel. Programmable lock allows for personalized security codes, one-time use codes, and access logs. Uses hull rating when contested.

(E) Gravitic Field Generator.name: (E) Gravitic Field Generator
(E) Gravitic Field Generator.description: Creates a large gravitic field extending ship to ship. Can be used to grapple or tow. Temperamental and dangerous. Guild prototype. Not legal.

(W) Grappling Hooks.name: (W) Grappling Hooks
(W) Grappling Hooks.description: Officially for latching onto asteroids and netting cargo, it's an array of nets, grappling lines, and arms that can tie together two vessels for towing or boarding. Legal.

(U) Shuttle.name: (U) Shuttle
(U) Shuttle.description: A small spacecraft capable of carrying a few people from planet to orbit. Limited systems capacity - treat any system as quality zero vs. actual ships. Can attach to airlocks, but best stored in a landing bay if you don't want stray asteroids or partical cannon fire affecting it.

(Ce) Personal Vehicles.name: (Ce) Personal Vehicles
(Ce) Personal Vehicles.description: Your crew has a few (perhaps one per crew member) sleek single-seater craft that can fold up tight enough to fit into a reasonable parking space. Limited fuel, but can break atmo. Can carry basic weapons, though they can't seriously damage anything freighter-sized or larger. You may want a landing bay on your ship.

(H) Smuggling Compartments.name: (H) Smuggling Compartments
(H) Smuggling Compartments.description: Like a cargo hold (can carry a small shipment), but it won't show up on routine scans or visual inspections of the ship. At 3+ hull rating, has life support for smuggling people too.

(T) Playbook.name: (T) Playbook
(T) Playbook.description: May represent an appropriate place on your ship, relevant manuals, or expert mentors. Mark 2 xp in the appropriate category instead of 1 when taking the downtime train action.

(G) Workshop.name: (G) Workshop
(G) Workshop.description: Plasma cutters, a nano-assembler, a stock of metal and electrical components, a forge - anything required to build, modify, or disassemble complex machines. Adds +1 quality to craft rolls.

(A) Medical Bay.name: (A) Medical Bay
(A) Medical Bay.description: A clean room with medical equipment. No hospital, but sufficient to patch most injuries. Storage for drugs and medical scanners. Add +1d to recovery rolls.

(U) Power Reserves.name: (U) Power Reserves
(U) Power Reserves.description: Batteries and energy supplies that can power the ship independently of the engine. Sufficient for a few hours of operation at minimal usage or a few minutes of full power. Acts as armor against power-related mishaps.

(Fi) Popular Support.name: (Fi) Popular Support
(Fi) Popular Support.description: It takes work to win hearts and minds, but your cause has supporters among the common folk. When you approach a planet or a station, ask the GM who there might be a sympathizer. This may make escapes (and simply walking around while wanted) much easier.

(A) Science Bay.name: (A) Science Bay
(A) Science Bay.description: Laboratory that can be used to analyze anomalies and Precursor artifacts. Secure storage for things that may react oddly with the rest of the ship (or physics).

(H) Crew Quarters.name: (H) Crew Quarters
(H) Crew Quarters.description: You can sleep anywhere, but crew quarters are actually meant for it. Crew quarters afford privacy and comfort in a domain where such things are luxuries. Also you don't have to share, and you know the first mate snores.

(A) Galley.name: (A) Galley
(A) Galley.description: A combined kitchen and serving area for meals. Greatly facilitates longer trips. Includes fresh food storage.

(C) Quantum Encryptor.name: (C) Quantum Encryptor
(C) Quantum Encryptor.description: Encrypts comms and system storage. Grants special armor against interception of digital communications. Data on the ship is in a secure state until unlocked.

(St) Thrillseekers.name: (St) Thrillseekers
(St) Thrillseekers.description: Each PC gets +1 stress box (increase stress max to 10).

(H) Landing Bay.name: (H) Landing Bay
(H) Landing Bay.description: Airlocks, bay-doors, and takeoff ramps to accomodate shuttles and single-pilot small fighter craft.

(St) Lucky Charm.name: (St) Lucky Charm
(St) Lucky Charm.description: Whether an Ur artifact or a few mementos prominently displayed on the bridge, sometimes luck is just about believing in something. The crew starts with +1 gambit every job.

(St) Smuggler's Rigging.name: (St) Smuggler's Rigging
(St) Smuggler's Rigging.description: Webbing or fake skin used to hold small items close to the body and a great way to sneak them past security. Adds some hands-free carry room while working on the outside of the ship, and lets you smuggle a blaster into a well guarded meeting while keeping the stylish cut of your coat. You can only carry/hide one item of a max of 1 load this way.

(G) Land Transport.name: (G) Land Transport
(G) Land Transport.description: Land-based transports for the entire crew. Tires or close-to-ground hover. These may be motorized bikes, land-skimmers, boats, or very small cars.

(U) Stasis Pods.name: (U) Stasis Pods
(U) Stasis Pods.description: State-of-the-art pods provide room for one severely injured, deathly ill, or unconscious guest each. Does not prevent dreams.

(Fi) Way Blessed.name: (Fi) Way Blessed
(Fi) Way Blessed.description: Some people are just plain lucky. The common folk think this is some sort of sign. Don't look too much into it. You start with +1 gambit at the start of every job.

(C) Fake Transponder.name: (C) Fake Transponder
(C) Fake Transponder.description: Usable remotely, this system can broadcast a different ship's signal or play a powerful recording or sensor echoes (or act as a beacon).

(W) Coherence Cannon.name: (W) Coherence Cannon
(W) Coherence Cannon.description: Capital weapon. One shot only until repaired or recharged on ships smaller than dreadnoughts. May fry systems. Deadly. Super not legal.
